Variables: Your Program's Storage Boxes

Stage 2 Concept ⏱ 15 min 📖 Glossary

A variable is a labelled lunchbox: one box, one kind of food, one name tag. Put things in, peek at them, swap them — the tag stays, the content changes.

🔎 Motivating questionIf your desk had 100 unlabeled drawers, how fast could you find your charger in the dark?

Objectives

  • Explain what a variable stores
  • Declare and initialize
  • Read and update a value

Needs first: Comments and Readable Code

1 Start with an analogy

Real life first, code second.

Labelled lunchboxes on a shelf. The type is the “soup only” sticker, the name is “Aarav’s” tag, the value is today’s soup. Swap the soup any day; the sticker and tag stay put.

⚠️ Where the analogy breaksWhere it breaks: real boxes accept anything. A Java box accepts exactly ONE declared type — a soup box refuses sandwiches, and the compiler is the canteen auntie enforcing it.

2 The concept, plainly

One idea at a time, words before jargon.

Declare with type, name, and a starting value: int age = 18; The = STORES (assignment) — it does not ask a question. Questions come later with ==.

Names start with a letter, use camelCase (userAge), say what they hold, and are case-sensitive: age and Age are different boxes.

Reassign any time: age = 19; throws away the old value and stores the new one — one box, one current value, always.

Every variable has exactly three parts — type, name, value — and the right side of = always computes FIRST, then stores. In x = x + 3, the old x is read, 3 is added, and the result moves back into x.

⚙️ Tech details — precise facts
  • Local variables MUST be initialized before use — Java refuses to guess, and the compiler rejects reading an empty box. (Fields get defaults; locals do not.)
  • Legal names: letters, digits, _ and $; cannot start with a digit; cannot be a keyword like int or class. Convention: camelCase, never snake_case.
  • int is the default integer choice; reach for long/double only with a reason — a theme the types lesson makes precise.

3 Watch it move: Lunchbox assignment

Step at your pace. Text explains every move.

4 Live code demo

Small, correct Java 17 (LTS) code. Read, trace, copy.

Main.javaJava 17
public class Main {
  public static void main(String[] args) {
    int age = 17;            // declare + initialize
    System.out.println(age); // 17
    age = 18;                // birthday: replace the content
    System.out.println(age); // 18
    age = age + 1;           // read, add, store back
    System.out.println(age); // 19
  }
}
▶ Output 17 18 19
  • Line 3 creates box age holding 17.
  • Line 5 overwrites it with 18 — 17 is gone.
  • Line 7 reads 18, adds 1, stores 19 back.
▶️ Run it yourselfSave exactly as Main.java, then javac Main.java and java Main. Every full program in this course works this way.
💡 Why this output?First print reads 17. Assignment overwrites with 18. The last line computes 18 + 1 and stores 19, which the final print shows.

6 Common mistakes (at least 3)

Wrong, why, fixed — learn from realistic slips.

❌ Mistake 1: int age; then printing age.Why: An empty local box — Java refuses to guess and the compiler stops you.
✅ Fix: Always initialize: int age = 0; then use it.
❌ Mistake 2: age = "old"; when age is int.Why: Wrong food in the box: text cannot live in an int.
✅ Fix: Keep the type: age = 19; — or declare a String box instead.
❌ Mistake 3: Writing = when you mean ==.Why: Single = stores; double == compares. Different jobs, different symbols.
✅ Fix: Store with =, compare with == (full lesson soon).

7 Guided practice

Hints first, solutions only after a real try.

Trace it

int x = 2; x = x + 3; print x. What shows, and why?

HintRight side computes first, then stores.
Solution5 — x + 3 reads 2, makes 5, stores it back into x.
Name them

Name and declare boxes for: the user’s city and their game score, with starting values.

HintcamelCase; types String and int.
SolutionString userCity = "Pune"; int score = 0;

8 Lesson quiz

3+ questions. Attempts saved locally; review queue learns your weak spots.

9 Takeaways + next step

  • Variable = type + name + value.
  • Single = stores; names are camelCase and case-sensitive.
  • One box holds one current value; right side computes first.
  • Locals must be initialized before reading.
🧠 Recall challengeWhat three parts does every variable have, and which computes first in x = x + 3?
